high_level_description: The image is a split-screen graphic that illustrates the boiling point of water under different conditions. The top half shows a pot of water on a stove, with bubbles forming on the surface, indicating that it is boiling. The text overlay reads: "Water actually boils at 10°C when placed 27km above the surface." This suggests that at high altitudes, where atmospheric pressure is lower, water can boil at a temperature below its normal boiling point of 100°C.
